Faithful details worth knowing: every measurement is the app's own — 52px hero top padding, 24px gutters, 24px/16px radii, the 62% check-in bar and the 7 dots are both hardcoded in PrototypeHero, and the seven dots genuinely compress to ~14px wide inside a 165px tile at 390px, which is what the real build does. Tailwind's grid-cols-* expands to repeat(n, minmax(0,1fr)), so I used that rather than 1fr. Layout verified in headless Chrome at 2x: content bottom lands at 761px, the floating pill occupies 758–820px, so the pill rests on the learn card's bottom edge exactly as it does on device.

Approximations and one deliberate omission:
- OMITTED: the hero's medication row. PrototypeHero always renders one of two variants there (a filled thyroid-medication reminder, or a dashed "Add your thyroid medication" prompt), and both name medication, which the brief forbids outright. Removing it is the only edit to the real composition; it also happens to be what makes the rest fit 844px without clipping.
- Week 2 / Day 9: programWeek = ceil(elapsed/7) and dayOfReset = floor(elapsed)+1, so Day 9 and Week 2 are the consistent pair for a start date of 17 Aug.
- "5 exercises / Scheduled for today" is the todayFocus branch that fires when the coach has scheduled a session for today; the count is invented (the app reads it from her plan).
- Learn card shows the real week-2 lesson from data/lessons.ts (protein-first), which is what nextLesson() returns once the week-1 lessons are read. Chose it over the other week-2 lesson deliberately: the alternative is titled around TSH and would read on her home screen as a comment on her own number.
- Date string is the app's own en-IN format for today, 25 August 2026 (Tuesday); greeting is the pre-noon branch.
- Font stack keeps 'Satoshi' first as the app does, with Helvetica Neue/system-ui behind it since Satoshi is served from Fontshare, not Google. The two tile labels carry white-space:nowrap so a fallback font cannot wrap "Weekly check-in" onto two lines the way the real Satoshi build never does.

- app/dashboard/progress/page.tsx — the route; hands check-in rows plus start_date to ProgressView.
- components/progress/ProgressView.tsx — the real screen. Reproduced: the fixed teal .tw-glow, the sticky blurred header (rgba(9,12,20,0.8), 1px bottom hairline, ArrowLeft in #7e8a9e, "My Progress" in Instrument Serif italic), the centred hero moment (10.5px/0.16em uppercase eyebrow → Instrument Serif italic number with textShadow 0 0 44px rgba(45,212,191,0.35) → 12.5px #a9b2c1 line), the three-tab selector with the active tab as solid #2dd4bf on #04121a, the p-6 rounded-2xl cards at rgba(255,255,255,0.03) / 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.06), and the closing 11px #5a6578 note.
- components/charts/TrendChart.tsx — the chart idiom I hand-authored in SVG: area under a 2px line filled with a top-down teal gradient (0.22→0 opacity, softened to 0.17 here), min/max value labels at the far left in 10px #5a6578, the dashed target line + right-of-line label from the `band` prop, dot per point, and the three-part footer row (first label · delta · last label).
- components/coach/TrendChart.tsx — read for the same idiom coach-side; confirmed the dashed gridline treatment and 9px axis type (raised to 10px here for the print floor).
- components/charts/BodyCompositionChart.tsx — MetricBar is exported from here and is what the wellbeing view renders: 52px label, 26px rounded-lg track at rgba(255,255,255,0.035), fill as linear-gradient(90deg, color22, color) with a 0 0 18px colour glow, then value + delta right-aligned.
- components/dashboard/BottomNavPill.tsx — the floating pill: bottom 24, 10px/32px padding, rgba(9,12,20,0.75) with blur(28px) saturate(180%), 4 × 40px targets on an 8px gap, active pip rgba(45,212,191,0.15) at left = index × 48. Lucide Home / TrendingUp / Apple / User redrawn as inline SVG at their real 20px (22px active) sizes and colours.
- app/globals.css — palette and .tw-glow verified; app/layout.tsx — Instrument Serif via next/font, Satoshi via Fontshare, so I gave Satoshi a real fallback stack.
- lib/health/programme.ts — programme weeks are 1-based, so the axis runs W1…W12 rather than W0.
- components/dashboard/WellnessScorecard.tsx + lib/health/checkin-scales.ts + WeeklyCheckInFlow.tsx — where "Mental Clarity" comes from (derived from the stress score) and confirmation that energy / sleep are 1–10.

Approximations and deliberate departures:

1. The screen is a PROJECTION, so the hero could not use ProgressView's literal `${lost} kg down`, which reads as achieved. It reads "70 → 60 kg" under an amber "TARGET · WEEK 12 OF 12" eyebrow instead, with the same serif treatment and glow. Projection is signalled five times: the amber header pill, the eyebrow, the hero sub-line, the chart's dashed amber target line and ring, and the amber "WEEK 12 TARGET" tag on the wellness card.
2. The weight series is invented as a plausible plan (70.0 → 68.7 → 67.8 → 67.0 → 66.1 → 65.5 → 65.0 → 64.2 → 63.3 → 62.3 → 61.1 → 60.0), front-loaded then softening mid-programme. Drawn with a dashed stroke rather than the app's solid one — the app only ever draws recorded points, and a solid line here would read as history.
3. The wellbeing card renders as its own card below the tabbed one (the app's Symptoms and Milestones cards sit there) rather than inside the "How you feel" tab, since the Weight tab is the one shown. WELLBEING in ProgressView lists Energy / Sleep / Mood / Digestion / Nutrition; per the brief I substituted Mental clarity for Digestion, which the app tracks on the home scorecard. WellnessScorecard tints Mental Clarity #fb7185 — a rose. I did not carry that across: red-family on her body is out, so all four deltas use the progress screen's own improvement teal.
4. Label column widened from 52px to 76px so "Mental clarity" sets on one line.
5. Added a phone status bar (time + signal/wifi/battery). The app renders none — it launches full-screen with a black-translucent status bar — but a 390×844 mock needs one.
6. No labs, no symptom card, no medication reference, and no coach message anywhere on the screen.

Verified by rendering at 2× in headless Chrome: content ends well clear of the nav pill, nothing overflows 390×844, smallest type is 10px. Working files (throwaway) are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-swapnil-thyroid-premium-site/df2cdb23-31ac-4a44-b4f6-06ff42caf1fd/scratchpad/.

Traced: /Users/swapnil/Documents/thyroid-fatloss-app/app/dashboard/plans/page.tsx (page shell, header "Your Plans", #090c14 ground, max-w-2xl px-6 py-8, space-y-5 between the two PlanCards), components/dashboard/PlanCard.tsx (card chrome, 44px teal icon tile, Instrument Serif italic title + "Updated {d MMM}" in en-IN, the meal-item row: uppercase teal slot chip, name + smaller portion with the "{qty} × " prefix only when qty ≠ 1, right-aligned Math.round(calories*qty) kcal, 15px chevron; then the right-aligned teal "Day total ≈ … kcal · …g protein" line), components/dashboard/MealLogger.tsx ("TODAY'S MEALS" 10.5px/0.16em, the n/total counter, and the round done/undone pills built from the plan's own distinct slots), components/dashboard/BottomNavPill.tsx (floating pill, 10px/32px padding, 4 × 40px circular tabs on a 48px stride, active index 2 for /dashboard/plans, the 40px rgba(45,212,191,0.15) indicator), app/actions/plans.ts (MealItem shape), app/globals.css and app/layout.tsx (palette, Instrument Serif via next/font, Satoshi as the body face).

The food is real, not invented. I ran a faithful JS port of lib/plans/generate.ts against the live `foods` table (216 rows, queried with psql via .env.local) — veg, west-Indian cuisine, roti staple, 4 meals/day, variety 0, at the 1440 kcal target lib/plans/targets.ts computes for her (39 F, 150 cm, 70 kg, goal 60 kg, lightly active: Mifflin 1281 kcal × 1.375, −18%). The six rows shown are exactly that generator's output, including the composite lunch and dinner (carb base + protein main) and the portion multipliers from its QTYS ladder. Totals are the app's own arithmetic: 1400 kcal, 70 g protein.

Approximated / chosen, and worth knowing:
- Her food preferences aren't in the brief. I picked the most plausible set for a Marathi woman of her age (vegetarian, west-Indian, roti, four meals) — that choice, not the app, decides which dishes appear.
- Protein target: at the auto-computed 110 g the generator appends a top-up row (Greek Yogurt, tagged "Snack") after the dinner rows, pushing the day to 1490 kcal and putting a snack out of chronological order. I used a coach-set protein figure where no top-up fires, which is why the day reads Breakfast → Lunch → Snack → Dinner cleanly. Every plan is coach-reviewed before assignment, so this is a supported state, but it is a choice I made.
- Satoshi is served from Fontshare, which won't load here, so the body face falls back to system-ui. I measured the layout in headless Chrome at 390×844 with that fallback, which is what the print render will use.
- First paint is honest, not tidied: the meal card runs 101→816 px, so the floating nav genuinely sits over the second row of meal pills ("Dinner"), and the Workout Plan card below shows only its top ~8 px. Both are what the real page does at this viewport — the nav is `fixed`, and the long name+portion strings wrap to 2–3 lines because the row's name column only gets ~90 px between the slot chip and the kcal figure. I left that wrapping exactly as the component produces it.
- Nothing on the screen touches labs, medication or a future number. The only figures are the plan's own portion and calorie arithmetic.

sourceNotes:
Traced, all under /Users/swapnil/Documents/thyroid-fatloss-app:

- app/dashboard/health/page.tsx — the page is a thin server shell; everything visible comes from components/health/HealthView.tsx.
- components/health/HealthView.tsx — page ground #090c14, the fixed .tw-glow blob (top -150, left 10, 360x300), the sticky header (rgba(9,12,20,0.8) + 20px blur, 1px bottom hairline, ArrowLeft in #7e8a9e, "My Health" at text-2xl in Instrument Serif italic), and main at px-6 py-8 with space-y-5. Section order on this page is LabReportUpload → LabDeltas → LabGauges → Thyroid profile → Trends → Lab results.
- components/health/LabReportUpload.tsx — the upload affordance is reproduced verbatim: rgba(45,212,191,0.08) fill, rgba(45,212,191,0.2) border, 40px teal icon tile, "Upload blood report" / "PDF or photo — values read on your phone, never uploaded".
- components/health/LabGauges.tsx — the whole "Latest report" card: the date formatted en-IN as "10 May 2026", the zero-flagged subtitle "Compared against the range printed on this report.", the uppercase panel label at 10px / 0.14em, the row layout (name → serif-italic value → unit), the gauge geometry, and the closing "Ranges come from your own report..." line. Its status() function is why TSH carries no badge: inside the printed range the app is deliberately silent, and out-of-range would be amber, never red.
- lib/labs/parse.ts — TSH is the first TESTS entry and panelFor() puts it in "Thyroid"; the report's own printed range wins over the standard fallback, which is why 0.35–4.94 is shown rather than the built-in 0.4–4.0.
- lib/labs/extract.ts and lib/labs/dates.ts — confirmed the read happens on-device and the date is lifted off the report rather than defaulted to today, which is what justifies "10 May 2026" appearing without her typing it.
- components/dashboard/BottomNavPill.tsx — pill geometry, 4×40px circular icons, gap 8, padding 10/32, bottom 24. Its activeIndex falls back to 0 on /dashboard/health, so Home really is the lit tab on this screen.
- app/globals.css — verified --radius: 1.25rem with --radius-2xl = calc(radius + 12px) and --radius-xl = calc(radius + 6px) under Tailwind v4.2, so cards are 32px and rows 26px, not the 16–24px in the brief. I followed the source. Fonts confirmed: Instrument Serif via next/font, Satoshi via Fontshare (not Google), so the stack falls back to system-ui here and renders as it does in the app.

Approximations, all deliberate:

1. The three "not tested" rows do not exist in LabGauges — it renders only markers present in the report. I added them in the app's own row idiom (same shell, name dropped to #a9b2c1, "not tested" in #7e8a9e, no gauge bar, no badge, no chip background). A badge would have made an absence look like a finding.
2. The lab's name, "The Lab Experts", is not shown. LabResult in app/actions/health.ts has no column for it (only taken_on, the core markers, extras and source), so putting it on screen would have been a fabricated field.
3. Gauge percentages are precomputed from GaugeBar's real arithmetic rather than left to JS: span 4.59, pad = max(4.59×0.35, |1.77−2.645|×0.15) = 1.6065, min −1.2565, max 6.5465 → band 20.6% to 79.4%, marker at 38.8%. Rounded to one decimal for the inline styles.
4. First paint stops after the "Latest report" card. The next real section is the Thyroid profile card, whose fields are Medication, Dose and When taken — showing even a clipped sliver of it would have put medication on the page, so the screen ends at the card and the floating nav sits over open ground.
5. Icons are hand-inlined from the exact lucide-react 0.564.0 path data for ArrowLeft, Upload, House, TrendingUp, Apple and User. The framer-motion spring on the nav indicator is rendered in its resting position.

Rendered and checked in headless Chrome at 390×844, 2× device scale: nothing overflows, the smallest type is 10px, and the marker sits inside the shaded band left of centre.
